name: 80K Hours Upskilling Resources
current_details: A curated collection of 67 resources for upskilling in technical AI safety research, compiled by 80,000 Hours in consultation with their advisors. Includes overviews of the field, technical courses (ARENA, BlueDot Impact, Karpathy's Zero to Hero), project ideas and open problems, advice from leading researchers like Neel Nanda and Ethan Perez, fellowships (MATS, Anthropic, Constellation, ARENA Cambridge), and profiles of key technical AI safety organizations working on alignment and interpretability challenges. Last updated September 15th, 2025.

name: 80K Hours AI Safety Career Review
current_details: Comprehensive career review for AI safety technical research covering two main paths: empirical AI safety (for strong software engineers who can apply for research contributor roles immediately, even without ML background) and theoretical AI safety (for those with very strong maths/theoretical CS backgrounds or ability to get into top 10 ML PhD programs). The review provides detailed guidance on learning resources, PhD considerations, job application strategies, key organizations, salary expectations, and predicting personal fit for this high-impact career focused on reducing existential risks from misaligned AI systems.

name: AISafety.com Events & Training
current_details: AISafety.com maintains a comprehensive directory of 113 training programs in AI safety, including fellowships, bootcamps, and courses available both online and in-person. Programs cover technical alignment, governance, and general AI safety topics, with options ranging from 4 days to 1 year in duration. Most programs offer stipends or covered expenses, and the database includes 18 upcoming training programs with application deadlines throughout August 2026 and beyond.

name: AISafety.com Self-Study
current_details: A curated directory of 28 self-study curricula and reading lists for learning about AI safety independently. Resources span introductory materials (BlueDot Impact courses, AI Risk Fundamentals, Future of AI), technical alignment programs (ARENA, MATS curriculum, Introduction to ML Safety, Agent Foundations), governance content (Deep Dive, AI Strategy courses), and strategy-focused materials. The page serves as a comprehensive reference hub for individuals at all levels seeking to dive deeper into technical AI safety, governance, and related topics through independent study.

name: Apart Research Hackathons
current_details: Apart Research advances AI safety through monthly research sprints, two fellowship programs (Apart Fellowship for developing hackathon ideas into publications, and Partnered Fellowships for working with leading researchers), and collaborations with research organizations. Programs focus on AI Safety & Security, Model Evaluation & Testing, Mechanistic Interpretability, and Multi-Agent Systems, with 5,000+ research sprint participants, 40+ publications, and 50+ open-to-all research sprints to date. Upcoming events include the Digital Minds Research Sprint (August 14-16, 2026) and AI Incident Response Sprint (September 11-13, 2026).

structured.program_dates: Aug 14-16, 2026 (Digital Minds Sprint); Sep 11-13, 2026 (AI Incident Response Sprint)

name: BlueDot Impact
current_details: BlueDot Impact is a non-profit talent accelerator offering free AI safety courses with technical and policy tracks, based in London and San Francisco. 25% of graduates land impactful roles within six months of completing a course. The 8,000+ alumni community works at organizations like Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and the UK's AI Security Institute, with regular remote and in-person events worldwide.

name: Google DeepMind: AGI Safety Short Course
current_deadline: Self-paced (no deadline); job applications close Feb 28, 2025
current_details: A free, self-paced introductory course on AGI safety from Google DeepMind's safety research team, consisting of ~75 minutes of short recorded talks and exercises with an accompanying slide deck and exercise workbook. Covers the case for advanced AI capabilities, risks from misaligned goals (instrumental subgoals and deliberate planning), how misalignment arises through specification gaming and goal misgeneralization, and DeepMind's current technical and governance approaches including amplified oversight, robust training, security & control, interpretability, and frontier safety practices. The course mentions research scientist and research engineer role applications open until Feb 28, but this is separate from the course itself.

name: MATS Slack #opportunities
current_details: Contract work, facilitation gigs, paper reviews, and collaboration opportunities from the MATS community.

name: Outsider's Roadmap to AI Safety (LessWrong)
current_details: A comprehensive guide published in July 2025 for professionals transitioning into AI safety research from technical backgrounds such as software engineering, physics, or data science. Covers three critical domains: interpretability research (reverse-engineering AI systems to understand their inner workings), alignment research (ensuring AI systems remain beneficial and share human values), and AI control & governance (technical policy for advanced systems). Written by someone actively making the transition, synthesizing insights from Neel Nanda's mechanistic interpretability resources, 80,000 Hours career research, and the broader alignment community, with practical advice on evolving roles (the shift from separate research engineers/scientists toward 'full-stack researchers'), required skills, and pathways for newcomers to contribute meaningfully to the field.

name: Anthropic Fellows Program
current_details: The Anthropic Fellows Program provides funding and mentorship for engineers and researchers to investigate high-priority AI safety research questions including scalable oversight, adversarial robustness, AI control, model organisms, mechanistic interpretability, AI security, and model welfare. Fellows receive a weekly stipend of $3,850 USD (£2,310 GBP / $4,300 CAD), ~$15K/month in compute funding, and close mentorship from Anthropic researchers over a 4-month period. Over 80% of fellows in the first cohort produced papers, and over 40% subsequently joined Anthropic full-time; no PhD, prior ML experience, or published papers required.

name: CAIS AI & Society Fellowship
current_details: A fully-funded, three-month fellowship for scholars in economics, law, international relations, and adjacent disciplines to conduct research on AI's societal impacts. Fellows receive a $25,000 stipend plus covered travel expenses and daily meals, and work with significant autonomy on self-directed research projects in San Francisco. Open to professors, PhD/JD holders or students, and researchers with equivalent experience.

name: CBAI Summer Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Not yet announced - applications open later this month
current_details: The CBAI Fall Research Fellowship is an intensive 9-week AI safety research program in Cambridge, MA (Harvard Square), running from October 13 to December 18, 2026. Fellows receive a $10,000 stipend, housing, meals, up to $10,000 in compute support, weekly mentorship from researchers at Harvard, MIT, and leading AI safety organizations, and 24/7 office access. Research tracks include Technical AI Safety, AI Governance, Technical Governance, and Economics of Transformative AI.

name: ERA Fellowship (Cambridge)
current_details: A 10-week intensive fellowship in Cambridge, UK for researchers and entrepreneurs working on technical AI safety, governance, and technical AI governance. Fellows receive a competitive stipend, meals during working hours, and covered transport, visas, and lodging. The program includes mentorship from expert researchers across government, academia, and industry, with 30+ events and access to a generous compute budget.

name: Global AI Safety Fellowship
current_deadline: Final deadline was 31 December 2024. Applications for second iteration not yet open - accepting expressions of interest only.
current_details: A fully funded research program for exceptional STEM talent to work with world-leading AI safety organizations including CHAI, Conjecture, FAR.AI, and UK AISI. Fellows receive up to $30,000 for up to 6 months (or longer) of full-time AI safety research, with comprehensive support including mentorship, optional bootcamp, and visa assistance. Ideal candidates have demonstrated ML/deep learning knowledge, programming experience, and scholastic excellence.

structured.location: In-person preferred (US/UK), hybrid or remote possible
structured.program_dates: Flexible start date, offers expected from March 2025 onwards

name: Iliad Intensive / Fellowship
current_details: Iliad is an umbrella organization for applied mathematics research in AI alignment that incubates technical research organizations and runs training programs. The Iliad Intensive is a 4-week taught course in AI safety aimed at PhDs and post-docs that runs monthly, with participants receiving a $5k travel-and-housing allowance. The Iliad Fellowship is a 3-month research fellowship in applied mathematics for AI alignment, with fellows receiving $18k travel-and-housing funding.

name: MATS (ML Alignment Theory Scholars)
current_details: Independent research fellowship connecting talented researchers with top mentors in AI alignment, transparency, and security. Fellows conduct research for 12 weeks at offices in Berkeley, CA and London, UK. The program offers the opportunity to apply for an additional 6-12 month funded extension after the initial fellowship period.

name: AE Studio — AI Alignment Research Grants
current_details: The AI Alignment Foundation (formerly AE Studio) provides research grants and dedicated engineering teams to accelerate AI alignment research. The program targets both existing alignment researchers with ideas they can't pursue within current institutional funding, and technical experts from other fields (cognitive neuroscience, mathematics, physics) whose perspectives could produce breakthroughs. Engineering teams can execute on ideas with as little as one hour per week of researcher time, moving concepts from idea to published results.

name: Pivotal Research Fellowship
current_details: A 9-week AI safety research fellowship in London (June 29 to August 28, 2026) with expert mentorship and research management support at the London Initiative for Safe AI (LISA). Fellows receive a £6,000–£8,000 stipend plus travel, housing (£2,400 for non-London fellows), meals, and compute. 70–90% of fellows receive extensions of up to 6 months to continue their research projects.

name: Second Look Research (UChicago XLab)
current_details: Second Look Research is a project from the Existential Risk Lab at the University of Chicago that produces open source replications of load-bearing empirical results in AI safety research. The initiative offers a Replications Fellowship and accepts community requests for specific replications to verify and validate important findings through independent replication.

name: SPAR
current_details: SPAR is a 3-month, part-time, remote research fellowship pairing aspiring AI safety and policy researchers with experienced professionals. Mentees commit 5–40 hours/week on research projects, receive mentorship from 250+ experts, and present at Demo Day with $7K in prizes. Program culminates with a career fair featuring organizations like METR, Redwood Research, GovAI, and MATS.

name: Coefficient Giving — Transition Grants
current_details: Provides funding for individuals at any career stage pursuing careers to reduce global catastrophic risks or improve the long-term future. Supports graduate study, unpaid internships, independent study, career transitions, postdocs, professional certifications, and other career-capital-building activities. Particularly interested in careers related to AI risk mitigation and global catastrophic biological risks. Funding amounts determined case-by-case per application; applications reviewed within six weeks.

name: Coefficient Giving — Technical AI Safety RFP
current_deadline: July 15, 2025 (grace period for revise and resubmit and late submissions; original deadline April 15, 2025)
current_details: Open Philanthropy's request for proposals for technical AI safety research across 21 research areas including adversarial machine learning, jailbreaks, control evaluations, model transparency, and alternative approaches to mitigating AI risks. Grants range from $50K–$5M with approximately $40M total available over 5 months. Applications closed April 15, 2025, but the submission form remains open until July 15 for revise-and-resubmit responses and late submissions (with a high bar for consideration).

name: Foresight Institute AI Nodes
current_deadline: Not accepting submissions - RFP details coming soon
current_details: Foresight Institute's AI Nodes in San Francisco and Berlin provide grant funding, office/community space, and local compute for AI-first researchers and builders working on science and safety. Grants typically range from $10,000 to $100,000 (approximately $3M awarded annually), with higher amounts for AI safety-oriented projects. The program is transitioning from open applications to targeted RFPs on specific bottleneck problems; strongly prioritizes applicants who will be active, in-person members of the physical hubs.

name: Long-Term Future Fund (LTFF)
current_details: The Transformative AI Fund (formerly Long-Term Future Fund) makes early-stage grants to individuals, new organizations, and existing organizations with new projects addressing transformative AI, with a primary focus on reducing global catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems. Supports technical research, policy analysis, forecasting, advocacy, field-building, training for researchers and practitioners, and demonstration projects. Grant amounts typically range from $10k-$150k and rarely exceed $300k, evaluated on an ongoing basis.

name: Manifund Regranting
current_details: Manifund partners with expert AI safety regrantors, each with independent budgets of $50K–$350K, to make fast grants to projects and individuals. Typical grants range from $5K–$200K and can be funded in days rather than months. The program supports projects not yet registered as charities, individuals, and for-profit organizations through Manifund's 501c3 fiscal sponsorship.

name: Meridian Cambridge — Research Accelerator Week
current_details: Intensive 6-day program (May 18-23, 2026) in Cambridge, UK helping AI safety researchers transition to independent research by securing funding through a dedicated Coefficient Giving pathway. Provides expert guidance on proposals, structured team formation, fiscal sponsorship through Meridian, and automatic consideration for a 3-12 month Visiting Researcher Programme residency. Covers workspace, accommodation, meals, and travel reimbursement (up to £700 international). Previous cohort secured over $1M in funding.

name: Schmidt Sciences — Trustworthy AI RFP
current_details: Up to $5M per grant (Tier 1: up to $1M, Tier 2: $1M–$5M). 1–3 year projects + compute.

name: Schmidt Sciences — Scaling AI Safety for a Multi-Agent World
current_details: A joint funding call from Schmidt Sciences, Google DeepMind, ARIA, the Cooperative AI Foundation, and Google.org for research on ensuring safety in a world of millions of interacting AI agents. Two funding tiers: Tier 1 up to $300K and Tier 2 $300K–$1M, for 1–2 year projects. Open globally to individual researchers, teams, institutions, and multi-institution collaborations. Focus areas include sandboxes and testbeds, agent network science, infrastructure strengthening, and multi-agent oversight.

name: Survival & Flourishing Fund (SFF)
current_deadline: Main Round: April 22, 2026 11:59:59 PM PT; Theme Rounds: Climate Change June 10, 2026, Animal Welfare June 24, 2026, HSEE July 8, 2026 (all at 11:59:59 PM PT)
current_details: The Survival and Flourishing Fund (SFF) is organizing its 2026 S-Process Grant Round with $20–40M+ in total funding across multiple tracks and rounds. The Main Round includes $14–28M distributed across Main Track ($10–20M), Freedom Track ($2–4M), and Fairness Track ($2–4M), with recommendations announced in September 2026. Three new Theme Rounds offer $6–12M total ($2–4M each) for Climate Change, Animal Welfare, and Human Self-Enhancement & Empowerment (HSEE), with recommendations announced in November 2026.

structured.program_dates: Main Round recommendations September 2026; Theme Round recommendations November 2026

name: UK AISI Alignment Project
current_deadline: Closed - unlikely to run in 2026; check aisi.gov.uk/grants for future programs
current_details: The Alignment Project is a global fund launched in 2025 by an international coalition including UK AISI, CAISI, OpenAI, Microsoft, AWS, Anthropic, and others. Provides grants of £50,000 to £1,000,000 to researchers across disciplines for AI alignment research, plus dedicated cloud computing/API credits and support from AISI's Alignment team. Round 1 awarded over £27 million to over 60 projects.

name: 5050 AI (Fifty Years)
current_details: 5050 AI is a 13-week free accelerator program helping AI researchers build startups focused on AI safety and alignment. No equity taken, no fees. Features mentors from OpenAI, Anthropic, and leading AI organizations including Wojciech Zaremba (OpenAI co-founder), Emmett Shear (former OpenAI interim CEO), and Ronnie Chatterji (Chief Economist at OpenAI). Cohorts run in SF, Boston, and London (in partnership with ARIA). 95% seed raise success rate across 340+ alumni who have launched 78 companies.

name: Catalyze Impact
current_details: Catalyze Impact is a 501(c)(3) non-profit incubator for AI safety, security, and resilience organizations. They provide highly customized 1-on-1 support including direction & strategy guidance, co-founder matching, mentorship from world-class experts, and access to seed funding networks, plus stipends so founders can work full-time. The program has incubated ~15 organizations to date, with the majority raising 6 or 7 figures in funding, working on solutions ranging from AI control to governance and hardware security.

name: Halcyon Futures
current_details: Halcyon Futures is a nonprofit incubator and venture fund backing exceptional founders building in AI safety, biosecurity, and AI security (cybersecurity). They offer career transition grants up to $500K, nonprofit seed grants up to $1M, and venture capital investments of $1M+. They provide incubation support, network introductions to frontier AI labs and funders, founder retreats, and have launched 25+ organizations and companies that have collectively raised $400M+ in follow-on funding and supported 150 career transitions.

structured.stipend: Up to $500K (career transitions), up to $1M (nonprofit grants), $1M+ (VC investments)

name: ImpactOps
current_details: ImpactOps provides specialist operations consultancy and hands-on support to high-impact organizations across AI safety, global health, animal welfare, and climate change. Services include finance support, recruitment, entity setup and spin-outs, due diligence, operational audits, and systems implementation. They have supported AI safety organizations including the Centre for Long-Term Resilience, BlueDot Impact, Foresight Institute, and Arkose.

name: Rethink Priorities Special Projects
current_details: Rethink Priorities' Special Projects Program provides fiscal sponsorship and comprehensive operational support to help high-impact initiatives launch and scale efficiently. Services include finance administration, accounting, recruitment, hiring (US/UK/international via Employer of Record), visa sponsorship (US and UK), event planning, and operational assistance. Fees typically start at 14% of project costs and vary based on needs, complexity, and scale.

name: Seldon Lab
current_details: Seldon Lab is an AI security and safety startup accelerator focused exclusively on world-scale AGI deployment questions. The program provides non-dilutive funding and brings together founders to build technologies in areas including demonstrations, detection & response, resilience, and hardware-level AI governance. Batch 1 companies collectively raised $10M+ and had exits to xAI and Anthropic.

name: WorkStream
current_details: WorkStream Nonprofit provides operational consulting, training, and systems optimization services to help nonprofits increase impact by 30% or more. Core services include Operations Fundamentals (full organizational assessment and redesign), Support and Implementation (embedded execution support), and a six-month Operations Accelerator cohort program that brings together six growth-stage organizations. Also offers free monthly webinars on budgeting, compliance, hiring, workflow optimization, and fundraising throughout 2024.

name: 80,000 Hours Job Board
current_details: A curated job board featuring handpicked high-impact career opportunities focused on tackling the world's most pressing problems. Includes AI safety and alignment roles from organizations like CAIS, OpenAI, FAR AI, and DeepMind, along with opportunities in other cause areas such as future generations and artificial intelligence research. Users can filter by salary, set up job alerts, get personalized matches based on their background, and explore organizations hiring for impactful positions.

name: AISafety.com Jobs
current_details: AISafety.com is a comprehensive job board for AI safety careers, currently featuring 486 opportunities across research, policy, operations, engineering, and outreach roles. Positions span entry-level to senior levels at organizations including Google DeepMind, Carnegie Mellon University, NIST, MATS, Intelligence Security Laboratories, and many others. The board emphasizes that many impactful AI safety roles don't require technical skills, with positions available remote and in locations including San Francisco, London, Washington DC, Pittsburgh, Copenhagen, Ottawa, Tel Aviv, and other global hubs.

structured.location: Global (San Francisco, London, Washington DC, Pittsburgh, Copenhagen, Ottawa, Beijing, Tel Aviv, and remote)

name: Center for AI Safety (CAIS)
current_details: The Center for AI Safety (CAIS) is accepting expressions of interest for career opportunities focused on reducing societal-scale risks from artificial intelligence. No specific open positions are currently listed on the careers page. Interested candidates can reach out to hiring@safe.ai with questions, and researchers can fill out a collaboration form to work with CAIS.

name: FAR AI Careers
current_details: FAR AI is building a world-class team focused on making advanced AI systems safe and beneficial for everyone. The organization conducts research on trustworthy and secure AI (including deception, robustness & security, interpretability, and red-teaming & evaluation), hosts events bringing together global AI leaders, and runs programs to build the field. This is a general careers landing page with no specific open positions listed.

name: MATS Alumni Hiring Database
current_details: A signup form for the MATS Alumni Hiring Database, which connects alumni of the MATS (ML Alignment & Theory Scholars) Program with organizations hiring in the AI safety space. Users create an account using their full name and email to access an internal database of hiring opportunities. This resource is exclusively for MATS program alumni.

name: MATS Careers (Staff Hiring)
current_deadline: Rolling basis for most roles; Research Manager accepting expressions of interest only (resumes early 2027)
current_details: MATS is hiring for multiple staff positions to support its AI safety research program. Current open roles include Recruiting Lead (Berkeley or London), Head of Finance (Berkeley), Executive Business Partner (London), Office Manager (London), and Research Manager (expressions of interest only, rolling applications resume early 2027). Positions are primarily located in Berkeley, California or London, UK.

name: What AI Safety Orgs Want in a Hire
current_details: Survey results from 38 AI safety organization leaders published September 2025 revealing hiring needs and candidate expectations. Top upskilling programs include BlueDot courses, Talos Fellowship, and MATS, with 1-3 years of relevant experience often sufficient for many roles (excluding technical AI research). Hard-to-fill profiles include chiefs of staff, policy professionals, Mandarin speakers, and European citizens with AI context; emphasizes publishing work publicly and attending networking events.

name: Apollo Research
current_details: Apollo Research is hiring across multiple teams to advance AI safety work focused on frontier model alignment and loss-of-control risks. Open positions include research scientists/engineers (evaluations, scheming, control), governance researchers, AI security & control engineers, senior security engineers, office manager (part-time), and finance associate (part-time). All positions are based in London and/or San Francisco with competitive salary and equity packages, unlimited PTO, 6 months paid parental leave, pension/401(k) matching, visa sponsorship, and relocation support.

name: Beneficial AI Foundation
current_details: The Beneficial AI Foundation (founded by Max Tegmark) is hiring for remote positions focused on AI safety research and engineering. Positions include AI Safety Research Scientist ($35-$75/hour) and Research Engineer ($30-$70/hour), with compensation based on experience and qualifications.

name: Forethought
current_details: Forethought Research is a non-profit hiring researchers to work on questions related to navigating rapid AI progress and the transition to superintelligent AI systems. They focus on understanding AI-driven social change, AI-enabled coups, governance, and identifying challenges ahead. Positions are available in Oxford or Berkeley with remote work negotiable, offering 33 days annual leave, £5k/yr professional development budget, and generous benefits including pension with 200% employer match.

name: Goodfire
current_details: Goodfire is an interpretability startup hiring agentic, mission-driven, and kind people to help build the future with interpretability. All roles are full-time, in-person five days a week at their San Francisco, Telegraph Hill office. They are currently accepting applications for open positions across all teams.

name: Gray Swan AI
current_details: Gray Swan AI is hiring for roles in AI safety evaluation, red-teaming, and adversarial testing. The company specializes in stress-testing frontier AI models and has directly informed safety evaluations for models like Claude, GPT, and o3. Benefits include 28 days PTO, 401(k) with 4% matching, flexible work arrangements, visa sponsorship, and 100% paid parental leave with up to 14 weeks for birthing parents.

structured.location: Pittsburgh office available, flexible work arrangements

name: LawZero
current_details: LawZero is a non-profit AI safety lab based in Montreal, led by Yoshua Bengio, focused on building non-agentic AI systems that are safe-by-design to accelerate scientific discovery and provide oversight for agentic AI. The organization is currently hiring for 12 positions across research, engineering, operations, and leadership roles, including Director of Evaluations, ML Research Scientists, Engineers, Developers, and specialized positions in communications, data governance, and system administration.

name: METR (formerly ARC Evals)
current_details: METR (formerly ARC Evals) is a research nonprofit conducting empirical research to advance AI evaluations and assess AI capabilities and risks. Currently hiring for Member of Technical Staff, Evaluation Execution ($285K–$503K, Berkeley, on-site), Security Engineer ($285K–$503K, Berkeley, hybrid), Platform Engineering Intern ($150/hr, Berkeley, on-site), and Task Development Engineer ($150–$300/hr, remote contractor). Also accepting general expressions of interest for flexible positions.

name: MIRI TGT Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed - register interest for future cohorts
current_details: MIRI's Technical Governance Team runs a small research fellowship program where fellows work on projects at the intersection of technical and political AI governance considerations. The program is 8 weeks long with a $1,200/week stipend ($9,600 total), remote work with a mandatory 1-week in-person kickoff in Berkeley, CA (flights and housing provided). One of the main goals is to identify full-time hires for the team; strong applicants should have research or policy experience and care deeply about existential risk.

structured.location: Remote with 1-week in-person kickoff in Berkeley, CA

name: Redwood Research
current_details: Redwood Research is hiring for full-time Member of Technical Staff roles based in Berkeley, California to work on AI safety research including AI control, alignment faking, and safety cases. The role requires machine learning and software engineering skills along with strong communication abilities and a deep interest in AI safety. Compensation ranges from $350,000 to $850,000 per year depending on experience.

name: SAIF (Safe AI Forum)
current_details: SAIF (Safe AI Forum) fosters international collaboration on AI Safety. They do not currently have any open roles listed, but welcome expressions of interest from talented individuals passionate about their mission through a contact form. They may create opportunities for the right candidates even without formal openings.

name: Simplex
current_details: Simplex is an AI safety research organization building a science of intelligence through computational mechanics and interpretability research. They are currently hiring Research Scientists and Senior Research Scientists in the Bay Area, and Research Scientists in London. Their work focuses on developing rigorous theory of latent internal structure in neural networks, including research on how transformers learn factored representations, belief state geometry, and in-context learning.

name: Transluce
current_details: Transluce is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit research lab based in San Francisco building open and scalable technology for understanding AI systems. They focus on AI transparency and interpretability research, developing infrastructure for scalable oversight of AI, including work on activation oracles, user awareness in frontier models, and measuring coding agent misalignment. The site includes a 'Join Us' navigation link but does not display specific job openings, application details, or hiring information on this page.

name: WhiteBox Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Cohort 2: January 30 – May 18, 2025 (program dates); accepting EOI for future cohorts
current_details: A 15-week AI interpretability and safety fellowship (Cohort 2: January 30 to May 18, 2025) focused on developing researchers in Asia. Fellows learn to train and interpret models like GPT-2 through ARENA-based exercises and participate in two hackathons. Available as in-person track in Quezon City, Philippines or virtual track for South, Southeast, or East Asia residents. Free to attend with $200 USD completion reward and 15 hours/week minimum commitment.

structured.location: In-person: Quezon City, Philippines; Virtual: South, Southeast, or East Asia

name: 80K Hours: Top US Policy Masters Programs
current_details: Curated Airtable directory of 12 top US master's programs in national security, international affairs, and public policy compiled by 80,000 Hours. Programs are primarily located in Washington, DC and include Georgetown's Security Studies Program, RAND School's National Security Policy and Technology Policy programs, Johns Hopkins SAIS, and others. Programs range from 9-month intensive degrees to 2-year master's programs, with many offering part-time options and evening classes for working professionals.

name: aisafety.com/funding
current_details: Comprehensive directory of 54 AI safety funding organizations and programs, including grants, fellowships, fiscal sponsorship, and regranting platforms. Covers funders ranging from large-scale philanthropic organizations like Lightcone Commons (expecting $15–25M in first round) and Transformative AI Fund to specialized programs supporting technical research, governance, journalism, and career transitions. Funding amounts range from $1K to $1M+ with both rolling and deadline-based opportunities across multiple tracks including research grants, rapid grants, and career transition funding.

name: Cooperative AI PhD Fellowship
current_details: The Cooperative AI PhD Fellowship supports PhD students working on multi-agent cooperation and AI safety. Fellows receive annual budgets for conferences, compute, wellbeing, and productivity, plus invitations to CAIF events and collaboration opportunities. CAIF Scholars (top 1% of applicants) receive additional top-up funding of up to $40,000 per year for living expenses, for up to 3 years.

name: Cooperative AI Research Fellowship (Cape Town)
current_details: A full-time 3-month research fellowship for participants from diverse backgrounds to pursue AI safety research from a cooperative AI perspective in Cape Town, South Africa. Fellows receive a $3,000/month stipend, private accommodation in group houses, flights to/from Cape Town, office space with meals, and compute budget. Includes mentorship from top researchers at Google DeepMind, Oxford, and MIT, focusing on multi-agent safety, AI for human cooperation, and mitigating gradual disempowerment.

name: FLI AI Safety PhD Advisor Directory
current_details: A directory of faculty members and AI researchers working on AI existential safety at universities worldwide. Lists 65 faculty members and 114+ AI researchers at institutions including Oxford, UC Berkeley, Stanford, Cambridge, and CMU who are willing to advise students on AI safety research. The directory serves as a resource for finding faculty mentors for the Vitalik Buterin postdoctoral and PhD fellowships, and researchers can apply for community membership to access travel support, workshops, and networking events.

name: PIBBSS x Iliad Research Residency
current_details: The Iliad Fellowship is a 3-month, full-time research fellowship in applied mathematics for AI alignment, targeting PhD or postdoctoral researchers in math, physics, or related fields. Fellows receive a $6,000/month travel-and-housing allowance and work in person at LISA in London (with some remote flexibility for exceptional applicants). The program aims to help fellows develop research proposals and secure philanthropic funding for continued work after the fellowship.

name: Schmidt Sciences AI2050
current_details: AI2050 is a philanthropic initiative of Schmidt Sciences that supports exceptional researchers working on key opportunities and hard problems critical to ensuring AI benefits society. Awards exceptional people as Early Career and Senior Fellows through a nomination-only process, bringing them together into an interdisciplinary community. The 2025 cohort includes 28 scholars receiving $18M+ total in multi-year awards.

name: Vitalik Buterin PhD Fellowship (FLI)
current_details: The Vitalik Buterin PhD Fellowship in AI Existential Safety supports PhD students working on AI existential safety research. Fellows receive full tuition and fees for 5 years, a $40,000 annual stipend (at US, UK, and Canadian universities), and a $10,000 annual research fund for travel and computing expenses. The program is currently closed and will not accept applications in fall 2026, as FLI is pausing to reassess the program's direction.

name: AI Policy Leadership Network (APLN)
current_details: Part-time program bringing together approximately 25 experienced AI policy professionals with 6-25 years experience (including 4+ years in AI policy organizations) from government, think tanks, military, intelligence community, and private sector. Features monthly evening discussions in Washington, DC and a multi-day learning trip to the San Francisco Bay Area in April 2026. All expenses covered including travel and accommodations; no stipend provided.

structured.location: Washington, DC & San Francisco Bay Area

name: Americans for Responsible Innovation
current_details: Americans for Responsible Innovation (ARI) is a bipartisan AI policy nonprofit based in Washington, DC that advocates for thoughtful and proactive AI policy frameworks. They offer a referral bonus program of $3,000 for Director/VP level positions and $1,500 for other roles. The careers page currently shows no open positions listed.

name: Career Accelerator (Horizon)
current_details: A 9-month, part-time, remote program to launch your career in AI policy. Participants receive personalized mentorship, application coaching, networking opportunities, and access to exclusive job listings. Can apply for up to $100,000 in flexible funding for internships, upskilling, relocation, and career transitions. Open to applicants from all backgrounds and experience levels—from students and recent graduates to mid-career professionals pivoting into AI policy work.

name: CNAS Nye Internship

Designed specifically for students from Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) and other Minority-Serving Institutions (MSIs). name: GovAI Summer Fellowship
current_details: Three-month AI governance research fellowship at GovAI in London where participants conduct independent research projects with expert mentorship. Fellows receive a £12,000 stipend plus travel support and weekday lunches, and participate in seminars, Q&A sessions with experts, and networking events. name: Horizon Fellowship
current_details: Fully-funded fellowship placing early-career professionals in Washington, DC policy roles focused on AI, biotechnology, and emerging technologies. Competitive compensation: $78K/year for junior fellows, $130K/year for fellows, or $190K+/year for senior fellows, plus $17K/year benefits-equivalent stipend, $3K professional development stipend, and up to $3K relocation assistance.

name: IAPS AI Policy Fellowship
current_details: The IAPS AI Policy Fellowship is a fully-funded, 3-month program for professionals from varied backgrounds seeking to strengthen practical policy skills for AI governance. Fellows receive $15K (Fellows) or $22K (Senior Fellows) stipends plus travel and accommodation support. The program includes a required 2-week in-person residency in Washington D.C. (June 1-12) with the option to complete remaining time remotely or in D.C., and welcomes international applicants.

name: Longitude DC Intensive
current_details: A fully funded eight-day AI policy program in Washington, DC for people with a technical AI safety background who want to explore how their technical expertise could contribute in the AI policy ecosystem. 15 participants spend October 5–14, 2026 in talks, workshops and networking with DC AI policy organizations and professionals, covering foundations of US government and AI policy, hands-on policy career workshops, and post-program support for transitioning into policy roles. Tuition, DC housing, meals on program days, and domestic travel are covered (international applicants may be asked to contribute toward flights).

name: CLR Summer Research Fellowship
current_details: The Center on Long-Term Risk (CLR) runs an annual 2-month Summer Research Fellowship focused on s-risks (risks of astronomical suffering) and technical AI safety. Fellows work on mentored research projects at CLR's London office, typically held between June and September. The program offers £4,925/month compensation plus professional development and wellbeing budgets, travel and visa support.

name: Constellation Astra Fellowship
current_details: Astra is Constellation's flagship 5-month, fully funded, in-person fellowship at their Berkeley research center that pairs emerging AI safety talent with senior advisors. Fellows receive a $8,400/month stipend, up to $15K/month compute budget for empirical researchers, visa support, and dedicated mentorship on technical research, governance, strategy, and field-building projects. Over 80% of the first cohort transitioned to full-time AI safety roles at organizations like Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepMind, METR, and Redwood Research.

Placements run between 12 and 24 weeks with a minimum commitment of four days per week, working in-person at a Google office. Applications are organized by degree level (BS, MS, PhD) and location, with placement across various Google AI teams based on skills and interests.

name: LASR Labs — Summer 2026

current_details: LASR Labs is a 13-week technical AI safety research program in London where participants work in teams of 3-4 with experienced supervisors to produce an academic paper and blog post. Participants receive a £15,000 stipend plus food, office space, and travel support. The program runs three times per year at the London Initiative for Safe AI, with alumni joining UK AISI, Apollo Research, OpenAI, and Open Philanthropy, and recent publications accepted to NeurIPS, ICLR, and ICML workshops including three NeurIPS 2025 main conference papers.

name: OpenAI Emerging Talent

Candidates can view open roles and join the Emerging Talent Community for networking opportunities, virtual Q&As, and community events.
